General.Description:
For three hundred years the Ember Throne of Keldrath has sat empty, its fire extinguished, its power locked behind a binding placed by the last of the Pyremancer kings. The kingdom that grew in the absence of a sovereign has become something proud and complicated — a republic of competing councils, merchant guilds, and military factions that hold a fragile balance through commerce and mutual suspicion rather than law.

Then the Throne ignites.

The fire does not choose a king or queen. It chooses Sable Vorn — a seventeen-year-old blacksmith's apprentice from the outer provinces who has never been to the capital, does not know who her parents were, and has exactly zero interest in ruling anything. The problem is that the Throne's fire will spread and consume everything it touches if it is not taken up by the one it has chosen. And there are people who would very much like it to burn.

The Ember Throne is a richly imagined epic fantasy debut that subverts the Chosen One narrative with wit, warmth, and considerable craft. Caelindra Foss builds her world in detail but never at the expense of her characters — and Sable Vorn is one of the most compelling protagonists the genre has produced in years.

A genuinely brilliant beginning.
